title: Counteroffer Blueprint & Escalation Cards
content:
Purpose: quick personal cheat-sheet for early-stage counteroffers and when to escalate to Legal/AE/CS. Not a final template — intended as a fast decision aid for deals <$250k ARR where we want speed but need to limit risk.

Top-level negotiation principles (one-liners):
- Preserve product access and logs for debugging; push hard on narrow data-use limits rather than broad carve-outs.
- Liability cap = primary lever. If they want higher liability, get equivalent concessions (insurance, indemnity carveouts, data residency).
- Avoid perpetual obligations (data returns/destruction): limit to transition window (e.g., 60–90 days) with a narrow forensic exception.
- Keep IP assignation: we own model outputs and service; customer gets use-rights only. If they insist on custom model IP, require compensation and explicit security controls.

Escalation cards (trigger -> immediate action):
- Subprocessor disclosure refused or blanket subprocessor clause -> escalate to Legal (must get list or right to object to critical subprocessors).
- Customer demands full source or production weights -> automatic escalate; likely deal-breaker.
- Unlimited liability / gross negligence carveouts -> escalate; require limited cap or remove carveouts.
- Data residency: asks for on-prem deployment or specific KMS -> escalate to Solutions/Eng for feasibility + SRE for network/security scope.
- Termination for convenience + no wind-down assistance -> add mandatory transition assistance clause or increase notice/window.

Clause watchlist & suggested counteroffers (short snippets):
- Indemnity: limit to third-party IP claims and exclude indirect damages. Counter: "Customer will indemnify for Customer Data and misuse; vendor indemnity limited to third-party IP claims arising from the Service as delivered."
- Liability cap: aim for 3x fees paid in prior 12 months or $1M floor; counter: "Cap equal to the greater of $1,000,000 or 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months."
- Data use / model training: prohibit training on customer confidential datasets unless explicit opt-in with compensation. Counter: "We will not use Customer Data to train or improve foundation models without explicit written opt-in and contractual terms."
- Export/residency: propose geo-tagged controls and SOC/HIPAA mapping instead of physical-only restrictions. Counter: "Customer data shall be stored and processed within agreed regions; for access outside region, Customer may request justification and controls."
- Security warranties: keep warranties timeboxed and tied to SOC/ISO attestations. Counter: "Vendor represents it maintains industry-standard security controls and will provide audit evidence upon reasonable request; warranties are limited to documentation and attestation availability."

Concession ladder (fast path):
1) Make a small pricing premium or committed capacity as first concession (low operational risk).
2) Add focused logging/retention assurances (shorter retention window) rather than broad data restrictions.
3) Agree to limited subprocessor transparency instead of veto rights (e.g., 30-day notice + objection only for critical subprocessors).
4) Engineering work (region/KMS) only as paid scoping + change order.

Communication scripts (AE-friendly, one-sentence):
- If customer asks for no-data-use: "We can lock down training/derivative use for your data — we treat that as a premium control; I can get you an addendum showing the exact language."
- If they push on liability cap: "We can move the cap if we can agree on a mutual indemnity and some contract-level safeguards like insurance — what's driving the ask?"
- If they ask for on-prem: "We support private deployments but that typically requires a separate engagement — happy to loop in Solutions to scope timeline and costs."

Red flags to avoid giving away:
- Broad assignment of IP in outputs or models.
- Unlimited rollback/forensic access without clear controls.
- Permanent deletion obligations without a defined proof-of-deletion process.

Quick-risk scoring (use when triaging):
- Low (green): commercial tweaks, liability cap within 1–2x, standard IP/data use language.
- Medium (amber): regional KMS, subprocessor objections, moderate requests on training data (we can fix with addendum + small fee).
- High (red): source code/weights, unlimited liability, regulatory mandated local hosting with no paid scope.

Open questions / follow-ups to log on the ticket:
- If customer requests dedicated KMS, what is current OSS playbook and estimated cost bands? (ask Infra/Solutions)
- For any indemnity carveouts, what insurance thresholds do we currently carry and can we share a certificate? (ask Legal/Finance)
- If they demand on-prem, what is minimum contract size and lead time historically? (ask Solutions Eng)

Notes to self / negotiation hacks:
- Use timeboxing: "We can pilot with a 90-day term and revisit data/training clauses after mutual usage evidence."
- Offer operational mitigations (audit log access, masked sampling) instead of product-level concessions where possible.
- Document every concession as a single clause in the change log — avoid scattered language across sections.

End: save this as a portable personal cheat-sheet. If we formalize, push top snippets into contract-template repo and add a short Confluence page mapping triggers to owners.

[handy snippets to copy into email/chat]
- "We will not use Customer Data to train our models without explicit written consent and a separate commercial agreement."
- "Cap on liability shall not exceed the greater of $1,000,000 or 3x fees paid in the preceding 12 months."
- "Vendor will provide transition assistance for up to 90 days after termination at then-current professional service rates."

-- end of notes --
